@nexxeln Tested this on Linux — the navigation logic and `subagents` memo are solid, but click-to-navigate on Task rows is completely broken because of the `renderer.hasSelection` guard.

**Root cause:** `renderer.hasSelection` (a getter on `@opentui/core`'s renderer) returns `true` whenever *any* text buffer has selection state — which in a TUI with rendered text content is essentially **always**. Every `onMouseUp` handler exits early on the `if (renderer.hasSelection) return` check, so `props.onClick?.()` never fires.

Confirmed empirically: instrumented the handlers with `Log.Default.error` calls — `onMouseUp` fires correctly on every click, but `hasSelection` is `true` on 100% of events (38+ clicks, zero `onClick` invocations).

**Fix:** revert all three `renderer.hasSelection` → `renderer.getSelection()?.getSelectedText()` (the original check). This evaluates whether there's actual *selected text content*, not just whether a selection object exists.

Affected locations in the diff:
- `UserMessage` onMouseUp (L1126)
- `InlineTool` onMouseUp (L1685)
- `BlockTool` onMouseUp (L1738)

+1 — this unlocks a big safety/UX workflow for me even with built-in agents.

## Use case: “auto-return to Plan” safety rail
I use `plan` as my default to avoid unintended edits, but I switch to `build` temporarily to execute changes. The problem is I often forget I’m still in `build` and send the next prompt assuming `plan`, which can immediately start editing/running commands.

This prevents accidental edits/commands by making Plan the “sticky default” after any Build interaction.

**Today I can almost solve this with a plugin, but it’s brittle:**
- on a user message sent under `build`, immediately switch the active agent back to `plan` for the next prompt
…but the missing primitive is exactly what this issue proposes: a deterministic, first-class way for plugins to set the active primary agent in the TUI.

## Request
Please add a plugin-accessible, deterministic “set active agent by name” mechanism (your `tui.agent.set { name }` proposal is perfect).

**This should:**
- update the TUI agent selector (so the next user input is actually sent as that agent)
- work for both built-in and custom primary agents

## Bonus (makes plugins more robust)
Bonus: emit `tui.agent.updated { name }` (or expose a `currentAgent()` API) so plugins can avoid redundant toggles and verify state.

This would let safety plugins implement “Plan-by-default” reliably without relying on `agent.cycle` ordering.

At my company, we would also like this functionality. Our use case is slightly different, but quite similar:

We have a custom provider (OpenAI compatible) and we have a small OpenCode plug-in that automatically detects the available models for that provider and adds them to the configuration.

We would also like to automatically configure the `small_model` used for session title generation. But only, when the user/employee actually uses our provider. There can be cases where they have other providers configured, too, e.g. for work for customers. In those cases, we do not want users to accidentally use a model from our provider, not even for session title generation.

At the moment, the selection of the small model is fairly rigid:
* use model of the title agent, if available
* use small_model, if specified
* use a „cheap“ model of the current provider (cheap is a hard coded list of model names), if available
* use gpt-5-nano of the opencode provider (if it’s not disabled)
* use the main model

What we need is _some_ way to control with a plug-in which small model is used when our provider is used, without impacting it for other providers.

I see a couple of ways of making that possible:

1. Add `small_model` as a per-provider option, too. The global small_model would still take precedence over this. This is basically what is described in this issue.
2. Add a way to configure a list of „cheap“ models per provider, that are considered as small models. This is similar to the previous option, but allows to configure multiple „candidates“
3. Add a plug-in hook for the title generation, that allows to select the model. Probably not the best idea because it is quite invasive. Just wanted to mention it for completeness.
4. Add a flag small to the model config options. Then, before searching for a „cheap“ model, we would look for a model of the current provider with this flag set to true.

I prefer option 1, but I'm open to explore the other ideas, too, if there is a preference for any of them.

Update: we've now also removed `source-path=SCRIPTDIR` from our `.shellcheckrc` and disabled SC1091 globally (PR marcusquinn/aidevops#2939). This eliminates the root cause on our side — even if `--external-sources` leaks through, there's no `source-path` directive to trigger recursive expansion.

However, the upstream hazard remains for other users: any project with `source-path=SCRIPTDIR` (or similar) in their `.shellcheckrc` will hit the same exponential memory expansion because bash-language-server hardcodes `--external-sources`. The suggested fixes in the original issue (OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP flag + SHELLCHECK_ARGUMENTS --norc passthrough) would protect all users.

Question: In your config example, you also specify the `model` per provider. How would that work? In OpenCode, you cannot actually really select a provider, you select a model. So the per provider `model` doesn't make much sense, to me. Or am I missing anything?
